original_value: Machine/Deep Learning (ML/DL) techniques have been applied to large data sets in order to extract relevant information and for making predictions. The performance and the outcomes of different ML/DL algorithms may vary depending upon the data sets being used, as well as on the suitability of algorithms to the data and the application domain under consideration. Hence, determining which ML/DL algorithm is most suitable for a specific application domain and its related data sets would be a key advantage. To respond to this need, a comparative analysis of well-known ML/DL techniques, including Multilayer Perceptron, K-Nearest Neighbors, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and Voting Classifier (or the Ensemble Learning Approach) for the prediction of parking space availability has been conducted. This comparison utilized Santander’s parking data set, initiated while working on the H2020 WISE-IoT project. The data set was used in order to evaluate the considered algorithms and to determine the one offering the best prediction. The results of this analysis show that, regardless of the data set size, the less complex algorithms like Decision Tree, Random Forest, and KNN outperform complex algorithms such as Multilayer Perceptron, in terms of higher prediction accuracy, while providing comparable information for the prediction of parking space availability. In addition, in this paper, we are providing Top-K parking space recommendations on the basis of distance between current position of vehicles and free parking spots.

result.paraphrase: Machine/Deep Learning (ML/DL) methods have been used on large datasets to extract useful information and make predictions. The results and performance of various ML/DL algorithms can differ depending on the datasets employed, the fit between the algorithms and the data, and the application domain being addressed. Therefore, identifying the most appropriate ML/DL algorithm for a given application domain and its associated datasets is a major benefit. To meet this need, a comparative study of well-known ML/DL techniques—Multilayer Perceptron, K-Nearest Neighbors, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and Voting Classifier (the Ensemble Learning Approach)—was carried out for predicting parking space availability. The comparison used Santander’s parking dataset, which was created during the H2020 WISE-IoT project. This dataset was employed to assess the selected algorithms and determine which one delivered the best prediction. The findings indicate that, irrespective of dataset size, simpler algorithms such as Decision Tree, Random Forest, and KNN outperform more complex ones like Multilayer Perceptron in terms of prediction accuracy, while offering comparable information for parking space availability prediction. In addition, this paper presents Top-K parking space recommendations based on the distance between vehicles’ current positions and available parking spots.
